Home / The evidence

This is not theoretical

Nigerian courts have already ruled on tampered pages.

The exposure is physical. A stapled or coil bound document cannot say whether it left your office in the state it arrived. The cases below are why that matters, and the figures below are what carrying the exposure costs.

The case law

Twice, at the highest levels.

FRN v. Ugwuowo (2020)

Federal High Court, Abuja

A lawyer was criminally charged for physically replacing pages 7, 3, 21, 23, 29 and 32 inside Supreme Court briefs, across four separate cases. The substitution was possible because nothing about the binding made it evident.

RCN Networks v. GTB

CA/L/888/2014 · Decided 18 June 2025

An entire ₦1 billion judgment was overturned because an execution page was allegedly moved between loan documents. The alteration was detected only through page numbering inconsistencies. The document itself could not testify.

The distinction most firms miss

Akpan v. Bob (2011) protects your brief from legal quality challenges. It is silent on physical integrity challenges.

If a page is alleged to have been altered, no case law helps you. No seniority helps you. Only the physical document can answer, and a stapled or coil bound document has no answer to give.

A question for the managing partnerIf opposing counsel alleged a page was substituted inside your filed brief, what is your firm's physical answer?

The digital tollgate paradox

Going digital did not retire the physical document. It promoted it.

Since the Lagos Federal High Court made e-filing mandatory on 27 April 2026, a paradox has quietly taken hold in every litigation practice:

  1. First service remains strictly physical.

    The originating processes that open a matter still travel by hand, in paper.

  2. Every legacy case runs fully manual.

    Years of live matters remain paper matters, end to end, until final judgment.

  3. The remaining paper carries all the risk.

    Going digital removed everything around the critical documents. The volume of paper fell and the value of the paper that remains rose.

The line to remember

E-filing handles the digital. CDIS handles the physical documents e-filing cannot touch, and those are the ones that matter most.

Also physical

Staples rust in Lagos humidity.

A document expected to last thirty years is assembled with hardware that fails inside one. The sealed record replaces the staple, the punch and the coil with a steel spine and a thermal seal.

Chain of custody

Six points where a bundle changes hands.

Between your printer and the court registry, a bundle is handled at six break points where interference is possible and detection is not. The free assessment maps them for your firm.

  1. The dispatch handoff
  2. The business centre stop
  3. The registry queue
  4. Post hearing reassembly
  5. The archive room
  6. The remote oath wet ink gap
